tasks.title: Orbit around your selection
tasks.hint: Select something, then hold the orbit button and drag - the camera turns around the selection, not around the view's own pivot.

tasks.title: Snap the view to a world axis
tasks.hint: Start the orbit drag first, then hold this key: as the view comes near a world axis it locks onto it and drops into orthographic. Let go for a free perspective orbit again.

tasks.title: Roll the view 90°
tasks.hint: Hold Alt and flick MMB in any direction - the view rolls 90° that way and lands squarely on the nearest axis view.

tasks.title: Slide the camera sideways
tasks.hint: Pan keeps the point under the cursor anchored, so the scene tracks your hand instead of drifting.

tasks.title: Zoom toward the cursor
tasks.hint: Point at something across the scene and scroll - you close in on that, not on the middle of the view.

tasks.title: Frame the selection
tasks.hint: Press it again without changing the selection to step through the cycle: bounds, pivot, close, then back where you started.

tasks.title: Jump to an axis view
tasks.hint: The numpad views: front, right and top, with the action modifier for the opposite side of each. NumLock has to be on.

tasks.title: Grab the selection and move it
tasks.hint: The selection follows the cursor across the screen - no handle to hit first.

tasks.title: Confirm a transform
tasks.hint: A left click or Enter drops the selection where it is and ends the grab.

tasks.title: Cancel a transform
tasks.hint: Right-click or Escape mid-grab and everything goes back exactly where it started - one undo step, never a half-applied move.

tasks.title: Grab-rotate the selection
tasks.hint: The same gesture for rotation: the angle follows the cursor around the pivot.

tasks.title: Grab-scale the selection
tasks.hint: And for scale: move away from the pivot to grow, toward it to shrink.

tasks.title: Drag an axis handle
tasks.hint: The arrows and boxes work as they always did - they just draw Blender's way, and honour everything this tutorial has taught so far.

tasks.title: Drag a plane handle
tasks.hint: The small square between two arrows moves along both of those axes at once.

tasks.title: Turn a rotation ring
tasks.hint: Switch to the rotate tool and drag one of the coloured rings; the angle follows the cursor around the pivot.

tasks.title: Drop an object onto a surface
tasks.hint: Hold this key while moving: the selection follows the surface under the cursor, for placing things on a floor or a wall.

tasks.title: Aim an object at something
tasks.hint: The same key while rotating aims the selection at whatever is under the cursor.

tasks.title: Snap to a vertex
tasks.hint: Unity's own vertex snapping: hold the key, pick up the selection by one of its vertices and drop it onto another object's.

tasks.title: Pin a virtual pivot
tasks.hint: Toggle it, then click a vertex to settle on it - drags snap from that point instead of a default origin, until you toggle the mode off again.

tasks.title: Drop the selection to the floor
tasks.hint: Rests each object's bounds on whatever is below it, ignoring its own colliders.

tasks.title: Constrain a drag to one axis
tasks.hint: During any drag press X, Y or Z. Press the same key again to switch between global and local; a third press on a G/R/S grab frees the axis.

tasks.title: Type an exact value
tasks.hint: Mid-drag, type a number and press Enter. The mouse stops driving the moment the first digit lands.

tasks.title: Lock a plane instead of an axis
tasks.hint: Hold this modifier with an axis key to exclude that axis rather than isolate it - the drag then runs across the other two.

tasks.title: Snap to the increment lattice
tasks.hint: Hold the action key while dragging to land on Unity's own snap increments; ticks are drawn along the handle as you go.

tasks.title: Slow a drag down for fine work
tasks.hint: Hold this key mid-drag: the selection moves a fraction of the distance the cursor does, and every snap step halves.

chapters.title: Scene Tools
chapters.subtitle: The rest of the Scene View

tasks.title: Isolate the selection, then leave
tasks.hint: Hides everything else while you work. The same key brings the scene back.

tasks.title: Step back through selections
tasks.hint: Browser-style back and forward for what you had selected - the mouse's own side buttons by default.

tasks.title: Step back through camera positions
tasks.hint: The same pair with the shift modifier undoes where you were looking from, not what was selected.

tasks.title: Click an axis on the orientation gizmo
tasks.hint: The ball in the corner of the view: click a handle to swing round to that axis, drag inside it to orbit, middle-click to toggle projection.

chapters.title: Pie Menus & Setup
chapters.subtitle: Menus on a key, and setup

tasks.title: Run a pie item with a flick
tasks.hint: Hold the key, flick the mouse toward an item and let go. Direction is all that counts - you never have to land on the button.

tasks.title: Latch a pie open and click
tasks.hint: Tap the same key instead of holding it: the menu stays up, and a left click runs an item.

tasks.title: Run a pie item by its number
tasks.hint: Every item is numbered; its number key runs it directly while the menu is open.

tasks.title: Open Blendon's settings
tasks.hint: Tools → Blendon. Every feature here can be switched off on its own, and its keys go straight back to the Editor.
